chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from his men, from Yunus, from them, peace be upon them, who said:

Regarding the hunut and shrouding of the deceased, he said: “Spread out the hibarah cloth fully, then spread the waist-wrapper over it, then spread the shirt over it, and fold the front part of the shirt over him. Then take powdered camphor and place it upon his forehead and the places of his sajdah, and wipe with the camphor over all of his folds from the hands and the feet, from the middle of his palms. Then he is lifted and placed upon his shirt, and the front of the shirt is folded over him, so that the shirt is neither hemmed nor buttoned. And place for him two pieces of fresh palm-stalk, each about a cubit in length: place one between his knees, half toward the shin and half toward the thigh, and place the other beneath his right armpit. Do not place cotton or camphor in his nostrils, nor in his eyes, ears, or face. Then he is turbaned: the middle of the turban is taken and folded around his head in a circular manner, then the excess on the right is cast over the left, and the left over the right, and it is extended over his chest.”

key_terms.تَحْنِيطِ: anointing the deceased with camphor as part of funeral preparation
key_terms.تَكْفِينِهِ: shrouding the deceased in burial cloths
key_terms.جَرِيدِ ٱلنَّخْلِ: fresh palm-stalk pieces placed with the deceased
key_terms.كَافُورٍ: camphor used in the ritual preparation of the deceased
key_terms.مَوْضِعِ سُجُودِهِ: the places of prostration on the body where camphor is applied
key_terms.ٱلْحِبَرَةَ: a wrapped outer cloth used in the shroud
key_terms.ٱلْعِمَامَةِ: the turban cloth wrapped around the head of the deceased

ai.seo_question: How should the deceased be anointed with camphor and shrouded according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the procedure for the hunut and shrouding of the deceased, including the order of the shroud garments, placement of camphor, use of fresh palm-stalks, and the manner of wrapping the turban. It is significant as a jurisprudential text detailing the prescribed etiquettes and rulings for preparing the deceased for burial in the Shia tradition.
